newsitem.title: UK: P&U Q1 sales hit by generic competition.
newsitem.headline: P&U Q1 sales hit by generic competition.

text.p: Pharmacia & Upjohn Inc said its first-quarter sales were hit by generic competition, while inventory increases in 1996's fourth quarter also had a negative impact on some products.
Sales in the health/urology business fell 17 percent, while there was an 18 percent decline in nervous system drugs and a seven percent fall in infectuous disease products.
Pharmacia & Upjohn earlier reported that first-quarter turnover fell to $1.6 billion from $1.7 billion.
The Swedish-U.S. drugs firm said its Xalatan glaucoma drug witnessed a sales increase of 25 percent, while Camptosar led a 28.5 percent sales rise in the oncology business.
But sales of two other anti-cancer drugs, Adriamycin and Pharmorubicin, declined, Pharmacia & Upjohn said.

Consumer Health Care sales fell 18 percent in the first quarter due to prestocking in preparation of the over-the- counter launch in the U.S. of a hair loss product and Nicorette Gum to help people stop smoking.
Animal health sales were unchanged, Pharmacia & Upjohn said.
